newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Anti-Mobutu protest cripples Zaire capital.
newsitem.headline: Anti-Mobutu protest cripples Zaire capital.

text.p: The Zaire capital Kinshasa was crippled on Monday by a stay-at-home strike called by opponents of President Mobutu Sese Seko, witnesses said.

Shops, schools, and businesses were closed and public transport was off the streets as were most private vehicles. Security forces were out in force in potential flashpoint areas, notably opposition bastions near the Njili airport. There were no immediate reports of incidents.

"There are troops just all over the place in the very militant areas," said a Western security official who toured the city's shantytowns. He said youths built a barricade in South Njilu district near the airport.
The business district in the city centre was deserted with a few para-military gendarmes manning key intersections.
A source close to the business community said business leaders, notably Lebanese shopowners, rejected a last-minute plea by the government late on Sunday to keep shops open.

Supporters of radical opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi, who was sacked as prime minister by Mobutu last week after only a few days in office, are spearheading the anti-Mobutu campaign in the capital. Mobutu's 32-year rule is also under attack from rebels who have seized more than half the country and have asked him to step down.
